newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - January 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - January 20.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
President Kumartunga said the government will proceed with devolutipn of power, despite objections by some members of the clergy and some newspapers.
Indian Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral begins four-day Colombo visit by attending third session of Indo-Lanka Joint Commission.

Sri Lanka Ports Authority warns workers that any attempt to disrupt policy of the government in the guise of trade union action, will be deemed sabotage. Some unions are against a plan to develop facilities through private sector involvement.
Navy to abandon search for missing Sri Lanka Air Force unmanned aerial vehicle, which disappeared last Thursday, defence sources say.
Health minister officials nab government doctor doing private practice during office hours.
Twenty-one police personnel and at least 50 Tamil separatist rebels killed in Kebithigollewa attack in north-central Sri Lanka.
The government, which got a 63 perent mandate from the people at the last election, will forge ahead with devolution of power, says President Kumaratunga.
